cover.body_html:
9月12日，硅谷最大的竞争对手们做了一件罕见的事：同一天，站在了同一边。

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei在公司官网发布了一篇超过5000字的长文——"We Must Pace the Frontier"。这不是一篇学术论文，不是一篇愿景声明，而是一份带着具体执行方案的行动纲领。几个小时内，OpenAI CEO Sam Altman公开表示支持，xAI（已被SpaceX收购后的SpaceXAI）和Microsoft也相继表态。同日，OpenAI宣布2026年不会进行IPO，并将这一决定与安全承诺直接挂钩。

一天之内，前沿AI安全从"大家觉得应该做"变成了"有人已经开始做了"。这个转变值得仔细拆解。

三步计划：从纸面到工牌

Amodei提出的三步计划，每一步都比前一步更具体、更难、也更重要。

第一步：嵌入式评估员（Embedded Evaluators）。这是整个计划中最具操作性的部分。Amodei提议，AI实验室应该允许独立第三方评估员获得与员工相同级别的访问权限——包括工牌、笔记本电脑、内部系统权限。这些评估员可以在实验室内部自由活动、审查安全流程、测试模型行为，并且有权随时公开发布自己的发现。

这与现有的"红队测试"有本质区别。红队测试通常是限时、限定范围的项目，测试结束即终止。嵌入式评估员则是一种长期的、持续的、有独立性的监督机制。他们的存在本身就是一种威慑——如果一家AI实验室知道每天都有独立评估员在看它的代码和决策，它的行为自然会发生变化。

Anthropic承诺率先单方面接受嵌入式评估员，这意味着不等行业共识形成，Anthropic就先在自己身上做实验。这是一个聪明的策略：如果实验成功，其他公司如果不跟进，就面临巨大的舆论压力。

第二步：民主国家行业协调。Amodei提议，AI前沿实验室之间应该建立更紧密的安全信息共享和协调机制——但这只在"民主国家"的实验室之间进行。这一步的核心障碍是美国反垄断法。竞争对手之间共享安全信息、协调政策，很可能被解读为限制竞争的"合谋"。因此，Amodei明确呼吁：国会需要为AI安全协调提供反垄断豁免。

这是一个大胆但必要的主张。如果没有反垄断豁免，前沿实验室之间的安全协调就永远停留在"自愿"层面，缺乏强制性和可执行性。Amodei等于在说：如果你们真的在乎AI安全，那就给法律开一道口子。

第三步：全球协调（含中国）。这是最具争议也最具远见的一步。Amodei承认，在AI安全问题上排除中国是不现实的——中国在AI研究上的实力决定了，任何不包含中国的全球安全框架都是不完整的。他提议探索一种包括中国在内的全球协调机制，即使这在当前的地缘政治环境下极其困难。

OpenAI的响应：不上市是安全承诺的货币化

同一天，OpenAI的回应同样引人注目。

Sam Altman在社交媒体上公开支持Amodei的三步计划，称其为"建设性的前进方向"。但更具实质意义的是OpenAI同步宣布的两项决定：

第一，OpenAI宣布2026年不进行IPO。表面上看，这是对"上市时间表"的推迟。但将这一声明放在Amodei的三步计划的语境下，含义就不同了。IPO意味着利润最大化压力、季度财报压力、股东利益优先。一个正在进行IPO的公司很难在安全问题上做出大胆的决策——因为安全投入是成本，短期内看不到回报。OpenAI选择不上市，等于给自己保留了在安全问题上"做正确的事"的空间。

第二，OpenAI同日发布了"针对前沿AI的安全要求框架"（A Framework for Safety Requirements for Frontier AI）。这份文件试图定义：什么样的AI模型需要接受什么样的安全审查？门槛在哪里？谁来执行？虽然具体细节还有待完善，但作为对Amodei呼吁的实质性回应，它比一句"我们支持安全"有意义得多。

"嵌入式评估员不是审计师，不是顾问——他们是拿工牌的独立观察者，有权随时公开发布发现。这才是真正的透明。"—— Dawn Vision编辑部

为什么这次不一样：从自愿到承诺

AI安全领域从来不缺漂亮话。每隔几个月就有一封"联名信"、一份"承诺书"、一场"峰会"。但这次有几个关键区别。

区别一：Anthropic率先单方面行动。以往的安全倡议都是"大家一起做"——这意味着没有人为失败负责。Anthropic承诺自己先做嵌入式评估员，这是一个可验证、可追踪的承诺。如果Anthropic真的引入了独立评估员并允许他们公开报告，这将成为整个行业的标杆。如果Anthropic食言，也会被迅速发现。

区别二：OpenAI用不上市做筹码。IPO对OpenAI来说是巨大的诱惑——数十亿美元的回报。OpenAI选择推迟IPO并将之与安全挂钩，意味着它在用真金白银为安全承诺背书。这不是口头支持，这是资本的机会成本。

区别三：计划包含了具体机制。嵌入式评估员有工牌、有笔记本、有权限、可以公开发表——这是具体的。反垄断豁免需要国会行动——这是具体的。全球协调包含中国——这需要外交突破，但至少定义了目标。与以往那些"我们将致力于安全"的模糊承诺相比，这份计划每个步骤都有可操作的路径。

挑战与未来：三步计划能走多远？

即使在最好的情况下，Amodei的三步计划也面临巨大的执行挑战。

嵌入式评估员制度面临的第一个问题是资金来源。谁来支付评估员的薪水？如果由AI实验室支付，评估员的独立性如何保证？如果由政府或独立基金支付，资金从哪里来？Amodei在文中没有给出明确答案。

第二个问题是评估标准。评估员"有权公开发布发现"——但"发现"的标准是什么？什么样的发现构成"安全风险"？谁来定义这些标准？如果没有统一的标准，评估员的报告可能沦为一场各说各话的PR游戏。

反垄断豁免更是充满了不确定性。美国国会目前在任何AI相关立法上都难以达成共识，更不用说为竞争对手之间的"合谋"开绿灯。即使在两党都支持AI监管的大框架下，反垄断豁免也会遭到许多议员的反对——因为它触及了美国竞争法的核心原则。

全球协调（含中国）的难度更是不言而喻。中美在AI领域的竞争日益激烈，双方在AI安全标准上存在根本分歧。让两国在AI安全问题上达成实质性协议，可能需要比Amodei想象的更长的时间。

但即使如此，这份计划的价值不在于它是否能全部实现，而在于它定义了一个方向。过去的AI安全讨论是抽象的——"我们应该怎么做"、"我们需要什么原则"。Amodei把讨论拉到了具体的机制层面——"谁来做"、"怎么做"、"做到什么程度"。即使最终的实施方案与Amodei的提议不同，这份计划也为后续的讨论设定了基准。

9月12日可能不会被铭记为"AI安全胜利日"。但它很可能会被视为AI安全从口号走向执行的转折点。当Anthropic率先让独立评估员走进办公室，当OpenAI用推迟IPO来表达对安全的承诺，当行业竞争对手开始讨论如何协调而非各自为战——这些细节比任何宣言都更有说服力。

AI安全的执行时代，才刚刚开始。

明天见。
cover.body_html_en:
On September 12, Silicon Valley's fiercest rivals did something rare: on the same day, they stood on the same side.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a 5,000+ word essay on the company website — "We Must Pace the Frontier." This isn't a research paper or a vision statement. It's an action plan with specific execution blueprints. Within hours, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman publicly endorsed it, xAI (now SpaceXAI after SpaceX's acquisition) and Microsoft followed suit. The same day, OpenAI announced it will not IPO in 2026, explicitly tying the decision to its safety commitments.

In a single day, frontier AI safety went from "everyone agrees we should do something" to "someone has actually started doing something." That shift deserves a close look.

Three Steps: From Paper to Badges

Each step of Amodei's three-step plan is more concrete, harder, and more important than the last.

Step One: Embedded Evaluators. This is the most operationally concrete piece of the entire plan. Amodei proposes that AI labs grant independent third-party evaluators employee-level access — including badges, laptops, internal system permissions. These evaluators can move freely inside the lab, audit safety processes, probe model behavior, and publish their findings publicly at any time.

This is fundamentally different from existing "red-teaming." Red-team exercises are typically time-bound, scope-limited projects that end when the test ends. Embedded evaluators represent a long-term, continuous, independent oversight mechanism. Their very presence is a deterrent — if a lab knows independent evaluators are watching its code and decisions daily, behavior changes on its own.

Anthropic committed to unilaterally accepting embedded evaluators first, meaning it won't wait for industry consensus — it'll experiment on itself. This is a clever strategy: if the experiment succeeds, other companies face enormous public pressure to follow. If they don't, the optics are devastating.

Step Two: Democratic Industry Coordination. Amodei proposes tighter safety information-sharing and coordination mechanisms among frontier AI labs — but only among labs in "democratic nations." The core obstacle here is U.S. antitrust law. Competitors sharing safety information and coordinating policy could easily be construed as anticompetitive "collusion." Amodei explicitly calls on Congress to provide antitrust exemptions for AI safety coordination.

It's a bold but necessary demand. Without antitrust exemptions, safety coordination among frontier labs remains "voluntary" — toothless and unenforceable. Amodei is essentially saying: if you truly care about AI safety, carve out a legal exception.

Step Three: Global Coordination (Including China). This is the most controversial and most visionary step. Amodei acknowledges that excluding China from AI safety discussions is unrealistic — China's AI research capabilities mean any global safety framework without China is incomplete. He proposes exploring a coordination mechanism that includes China, even though this is extraordinarily difficult in the current geopolitical climate.

OpenAI's Response: Not IPOing Is Safety Commitment Monetized

OpenAI's response on the same day was equally striking.

Sam Altman publicly endorsed Amodei's three-step plan on social media, calling it a "constructive path forward." But the substantive moves were two simultaneous announcements from OpenAI:

First, OpenAI declared it will not IPO in 2026. On the surface, this is a delay. But in the context of Amodei's plan, the meaning shifts. An IPO means profit-maximization pressure, quarterly earnings pressure, shareholder primacy. A company mid-IPO can't make bold safety decisions — because safety spending is a cost with no short-term payoff. By not going public, OpenAI preserves room to "do the right thing" on safety.

Second, OpenAI simultaneously released "A Framework for Safety Requirements for Frontier AI". This document attempts to define: what kind of AI models need what kind of safety review? Where are the thresholds? Who enforces? Details still need fleshing out, but as a substantive response to Amodei's call, it's worth infinitely more than "we support safety."

"Embedded evaluators aren't auditors or consultants — they're independent observers with badges, empowered to publish findings at any time. That's real transparency."— The Dawn Vision Editorial Desk

Why This Time Is Different: From Voluntary to Committed

The AI safety field has never lacked pretty words. Every few months brings another "open letter," "pledge," or "summit." But this time has key differences.

Difference One: Anthropic is acting unilaterally first. Past safety initiatives were always "let's all do this together" — meaning no one was responsible for failure. Anthropic committing to embedded evaluators first is a verifiable, trackable promise. If Anthropic actually brings in independent evaluators and allows public reporting, it becomes the industry benchmark. If Anthropic backtracks, that too will be swiftly exposed.

Difference Two: OpenAI is using its IPO as collateral. The IPO is an enormous temptation for OpenAI — billions in returns. OpenAI choosing to delay and tie it to safety means it's backing its safety commitment with real capital opportunity cost. This isn't vocal support; it's financial skin in the game.

Difference Three: The plan includes specific mechanisms. Embedded evaluators get badges, laptops, access, and publish rights — that's concrete. Antitrust exemptions require Congressional action — that's concrete. Global coordination includes China — that requires diplomatic breakthroughs but at least defines a target. Compared to the vague "we will commit to safety" pledges of the past, every step in this plan has an actionable pathway.

Challenges Ahead: How Far Can This Plan Go?

Even under the best circumstances, Amodei's three-step plan faces massive execution challenges.

The embedded evaluator program's first problem is funding. Who pays the evaluators? If labs pay, how is independence guaranteed? If government or an independent fund pays, where does the money come from? Amodei doesn't provide clear answers.

The second problem is evaluation standards. Evaluators can "publish findings" — but what counts as a "finding"? What constitutes a "safety risk"? Who defines these standards? Without unified criteria, evaluator reports risk devolving into a PR game of dueling narratives.

Antitrust exemptions face enormous uncertainty. Congress can barely reach consensus on any AI-related legislation, let alone greenlight "collusion" among competitors. Even under a broad framework where both parties support AI regulation, antitrust exemptions will face fierce opposition — they strike at the core principles of American competition law.

The difficulty of global coordination (including China) is self-evident. U.S.-China AI competition intensifies daily, with fundamental disagreements on AI safety standards. Reaching substantive agreements between the two nations on AI safety may take far longer than Amodei imagines.

But even so, the plan's value lies not in whether it's fully implemented, but in the direction it defines. Past AI safety discussions were abstract — "what should we do" and "what principles do we need." Amodei pulled the discussion into specific mechanisms — "who does it," "how it's done," and "to what degree." Even if the final implementation differs from Amodei's proposal, this plan sets the baseline for all future discussion.

September 12 may not be remembered as "AI Safety Victory Day." But it may well be seen as the inflection point when AI safety moved from slogans to execution. When Anthropic first lets independent evaluators walk through the door, when OpenAI uses an IPO delay to express safety commitment, when industry competitors start discussing coordination instead of going it alone — these details are more persuasive than any manifesto.

The execution era of AI safety has only just begun.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
又一轮天价融资，但这次数字会说话。

9月13日，智谱完成约50亿美元新一轮融资。交易结构包含两部分：约20亿美元的股份配售（定价714港元/股，较上一交易日折让约10%）和约30亿美元的零息可转债（转股价892.50港元，溢价约25%，2027年9月到期）。距上一轮约40亿美元融资仅隔数月，智谱在资本市场的"造血速度"令人侧目。

收入数据：从讲故事到算账

真正让这笔融资有底气的，是智谱同步披露的运营数据。

2025年上半年，智谱MaaS（模型即服务）收入达8.25亿元人民币，同比增长2736%。这个数字意味着什么？一年前，MaaS收入几乎可以忽略不计；现在，它已成为智谱的核心营收引擎。

更关键的指标：毛利率首次转正至24.6%。大模型公司亏损烧钱是常态，毛利率转正意味着智谱的商业化路径正在从"赔本赚吆喝"转向"可持续经营"。同期，Token调用量增长40倍，API平均单价上升101%——用户不仅在用更多token，还愿意为更好的模型付更高的价格。ARR（年化经常性收入）已达16亿美元。

融资结构：零息可转债的信号

这次交易的结构值得细看。

30亿美元的零息可转债意味着投资人在到期前不收取任何利息，纯粹赌的是智谱股价上涨后按892.50港元转股获利。25%的溢价门槛说明：投资人认为智谱股价至少还有25%的上涨空间，且这个判断要在2027年9月前兑现。

零息可转债是高增长公司偏爱的融资工具——它不稀释当前股东权益，不增加利息负担，但给投资人提供了上行空间。智谱选择这种结构，一方面说明它对自身增长有信心，另一方面也暗示：下一轮融资或IPO可能就在视野之内。

资金去向：自训练体系与算力基建

智谱表示，本轮融资将用于三个方向：下一代GLM模型研发、完全自训练体系搭建、以及算力基础设施扩张。

其中，"完全自训练体系"是关键。这意味着智谱正在减少对外部数据和外部训练资源的依赖，构建从数据清洗、预训练、后训练到部署的全链路自主能力。在当前地缘政治环境下，这种"全自主"路线不仅是技术选择，更是生存策略。

距离上一轮40亿美元融资仅隔数月，智谱在资本市场的节奏越来越快。当营收数据开始支撑估值故事，大模型的竞争就不再是"谁融得多"，而是"谁花得聪明"。

Another mega-round, but this time the numbers do the talking.

On September 13, Zhipu closed a ~$5 billion funding round. The deal has two parts: ~$2 billion in share placements (priced at HK$714/share, roughly 10% discount to last trade) and ~$3 billion in zero-interest convertible bonds (conversion price HK$892.50, ~25% premium, maturing September 2027). Revenue Numbers: From Storytelling to Math

What actually gives this raise credibility is the operating data Zhipu disclosed alongside it.

In H1 2025, Zhipu's MaaS (Model-as-a-Service) revenue hit 825 million yuan, a 2,736% year-over-year increase. What does that number mean? A year ago, MaaS revenue was negligible; now it's Zhipu's core revenue engine.

The more critical metric: gross margin turned positive for the first time at 24.6%. LLM companies burning cash is the norm — a positive gross margin signals Zhipu's commercialization path is shifting from "subsidized growth" to "sustainable business." During the same period, token usage grew 40x, while average API pricing rose 101% — users aren't just consuming more tokens, they're willing to pay higher prices for better models. ARR has reached $1.6 billion.

Deal Structure: The Zero-Interest CB Signal

The structure of this deal deserves a closer look.

The $3 billion zero-interest convertible bond means investors collect no interest until maturity — they're purely betting that Zhipu's share price rises above HK$892.50 for conversion. The 25% premium threshold signals: investors believe Zhipu's stock has at least 25% upside, and this bet must pay off before September 2027.

Zero-interest CBs are the preferred financing tool for high-growth companies — they don't dilute current shareholders, add no interest burden, but give investors upside exposure. Zhipu choosing this structure signals confidence in its own growth, and hints that the next round or IPO may already be on the horizon.

Where the Money Goes: Self-Training and Compute

Zhipu says proceeds will fund three directions: next-gen GLM model R&D, a fully self-training pipeline, and compute infrastructure expansion.

The "fully self-training pipeline" is the key item. It means Zhipu is reducing reliance on external data and training resources, building end-to-end autonomous capability from data cleaning through pre-training, post-training, and deployment. In the current geopolitical climate, this "fully autonomous" approach isn't just a technical choice — it's a survival strategy.

Just months after the last $4B round, Zhipu's capital market cadence is accelerating. When revenue data starts backing the valuation story, the LLM race shifts from "who raises more" to "who spends smarter."

briefs.body_html:
9月12日，微软扔出了一颗不太起眼但意味深长的炸弹。

微软宣布在Copilot for Word、Excel和PowerPoint中添加Grok模型，目前面向Microsoft Frontier客户开放预览，默认关闭，需手动启用。EU/EFTA/UK地区在预览期间暂不可用。这看起来只是一次普通的模型更新，但背后的故事远比表面复杂。

Grok的来历：从Musk的死敌到微软的室友

Grok来自SpaceXAI——这个名字需要拆解。2026年2月，Elon Musk的xAI被SpaceX收购；7月，合并后的实体更名为SpaceXAI。也就是说，Grok背后的AI团队现在隶属于SpaceX帝国。

这意味着什么？Musk曾是OpenAI最激烈的批评者，公开嘲讽微软与OpenAI的关系，甚至起诉OpenAI违背开源承诺。而现在，Musk的AI模型正通过微软的Copilot触达数亿Office用户。从死敌变室友，AI行业的关系网比任何剧本都离奇。

值得注意的是，Grok默认关闭——这意味着微软给了企业客户选择权，而不是强行推送。Frontier客户可以手动开启Grok，在Word中用于创意写作，在Excel中用于数据分析，在PowerPoint中用于演示生成。Grok 4.7即将发布，拥有2.1万亿参数，这个体量让它在某些任务上可能比GPT和Claude更有优势。

多模型帝国：微软的战略进化

Grok进入Copilot，是微软"多模型战略"的又一步棋。

一年前，Copilot几乎等同于"OpenAI的GPT"。但过去几个月，微软接连引入了Anthropic的Claude作为第二个模型家族，现在又加入了SpaceXAI的Grok作为第三个。Copilot正在从"OpenAI前端"变成"模型市场的聚合平台"。

这个策略的逻辑很清晰：不把鸡蛋放在一个篮子里。微软在OpenAI身上押了超过130亿美元，但如果OpenAI的模型在某些场景下不是最优解呢？多模型策略让微软可以在不同任务上选择最适合的模型——用Claude处理长文档分析，用GPT处理通用对话，用Grok处理创意内容。

对OpenAI来说，这是一个微妙的信号：你依然是最重要的合作伙伴，但你不再是唯一的选择。对Anthropic和SpaceXAI来说，通过Copilot触达数亿Office用户，是一个极具吸引力的分发渠道。

Frontier客户：高端市场的实验场

微软选择将Grok首先开放给Frontier客户，这个定位很有意思。

Frontier是微软的高端企业订阅层级，面向愿意率先尝试最新AI能力的企业。将Grok限定在Frontier客户，既控制了风险（如果Grok表现不佳，影响范围有限），又收集了真实的企业使用反馈。

EU/EFTA/UK地区的排除也不是意外。欧盟的AI法案对新模型的部署有严格要求，微软选择在合规审查完成前不向欧洲用户开放，是典型的"先美后欧"策略。

当微软的Copilot从"一个模型"变成"多个模型可选"，企业客户的AI策略也需要随之调整。选模型正在成为一种新的IT决策——就像当年选云服务商一样。而微软把自己定位为"不做选择的选择平台"，这个策略可能是Copilot最深的护城河。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
On September 12, Microsoft dropped a bomb that's easy to overlook but impossible to underestimate.

Microsoft announced the addition of Grok models to Copilot for Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, currently in preview for Microsoft Frontier customers — off by default, requiring manual activation. EU/EFTA/UK regions are excluded during the preview. This looks like a routine model update, but the backstory runs much deeper.

Grok's Origin: From Musk's Nemesis to Microsoft's Roommate

Grok comes from SpaceXAI — that name needs unpacking. In February 2026, Elon Musk's xAI was acquired by SpaceX; in July, the combined entity rebranded as SpaceXAI. That means Grok's AI team now operates under the SpaceX empire.

What does this mean? Musk was OpenAI's fiercest critic — publicly mocking Microsoft's relationship with OpenAI, even suing OpenAI for abandoning its open-source promises. Now, Musk's AI model is reaching hundreds of millions of Office users through Microsoft's Copilot. From mortal enemy to roommate — AI's relationship web is wilder than any screenplay.

Notably, Grok is off by default — meaning Microsoft gives enterprise customers choice rather than force-feeding. Frontier customers can manually activate Grok for creative writing in Word, data analysis in Excel, and presentation generation in PowerPoint. Grok 4.7, with 2.1 trillion parameters, is about to launch — a scale that may give it advantages over GPT and Claude in certain tasks.

The Multi-Model Empire: Microsoft's Strategic Evolution

Grok entering Copilot is another chess move in Microsoft's "multi-model strategy."

A year ago, Copilot was essentially synonymous with "OpenAI's GPT." But in recent months, Microsoft has added Anthropic's Claude as a second model family, and now SpaceXAI's Grok as a third. Copilot is transforming from "OpenAI's frontend" to a "model marketplace aggregation platform."

The logic is clear: don't put all eggs in one basket. Microsoft has invested over $13 billion in OpenAI, but what if OpenAI's model isn't optimal in every scenario? The multi-model strategy lets Microsoft choose the best model for different tasks — Claude for long-document analysis, GPT for general conversation, Grok for creative content.

For OpenAI, this is a subtle signal: you're still the most important partner, but you're no longer the only option. For Anthropic and SpaceXAI, reaching hundreds of millions of Office users through Copilot is a massively attractive distribution channel.

Frontier Customers: The Premium Market's Lab

Microsoft's choice to open Grok first to Frontier customers is strategically telling.

Frontier is Microsoft's premium enterprise subscription tier, targeting companies willing to beta-test the latest AI capabilities. Limiting Grok to Frontier contains risk (if Grok underperforms, blast radius is limited) while collecting real enterprise feedback.

The EU/EFTA/UK exclusion isn't surprising either. The EU AI Act imposes strict requirements on new model deployments. Microsoft choosing to hold off on European rollout until compliance reviews are complete is the classic "US first, EU later" playbook.

When Microsoft's Copilot shifts from "one model" to "multiple models to choose from," enterprise AI strategies need to evolve accordingly. Choosing a model is becoming a new kind of IT decision — just like choosing a cloud provider was a decade ago. And Microsoft positioning itself as "the platform where you don't have to choose" may be Copilot's deepest moat.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
解出答案和真正理解，是两件完全不同的事。25位全球最顶尖的数学家，刚刚联合向AI行业发出了这个警告。

9月11日，数学家陶哲轩（Terence Tao）在个人博客发布了一份声明——"A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics"，同步上线于mathandai.org。这份声明在一周内获得了25位菲尔兹奖得主的联署。菲尔兹奖是数学界的诺贝尔奖，每四年颁发一次，每次最多四人。25位得主联署，意味着全球近三分之一的在世菲尔兹奖得主站在了同一边。

核心指控：benchmark竞赛≠数学进步

声明的核心论点可以用一句话概括：AI实验室将数学问题作为benchmark竞赛，与数学学科的真实目标"严重错位"（severely misaligned）。

具体来说，AI实验室的做法是：选取已知有解的数学难题（如奥林匹克竞赛题、经典定理证明），训练AI模型去"攻克"它们，然后在排行榜上宣称得分提升。但数学研究的真正目标不是解出已知答案——而是提出新问题、发现新结构、建立新联系。

声明指出，这种benchmark驱动的AI研究正在产生一种危险的错觉：AI"解决"了数学问题，但并没有推动数学学科的真正进步。它更像是一个超强的考试机器，而不是一个有创造力的研究伙伴。

时间点的巧合：纳维-斯托克斯千禧年难题

这份声明的发布时间颇为耐人寻味。

就在9月8日，OpenAI刚宣布用1万个AI Agent"攻克"了纳维-斯托克斯方程千禧年难题。OpenAI称这些Agent在数小时内完成了对这一百年未解难题的"实质性推进"。这一声明在媒体上引发了巨大轰动——"AI解决了千禧年难题"的标题铺天盖地。

三天后，25位菲尔兹奖得主的声明来了。虽然没有直接点名OpenAI，但时间点的巧合让这份声明不言自明。用1万个Agent暴力搜索一个数学难题的"解"，和真正理解这个难题的本质，是完全不同的两件事。

超越数学：知识生产的预警信号

声明虽然以数学为切入点，但明确指出：这个问题不限于数学。

同样的错位正在发生于所有被AI"攻克"的领域——蛋白质折叠、药物发现、材料科学、代码生成。AI实验室用benchmark分数证明AI在这些领域"超越人类"，但benchmark衡量的是"解决已知问题的能力"，而非"推动学科前进的能力"。

声明认为，这对更广泛的智识工作构成威胁。如果AI研究的方向被benchmark绑架，那么真正有创造性的、非标准化的知识生产将被边缘化。数学家们担心的不只是数学的未来——他们担心的是整个知识生产体系被一种"考试逻辑"所扭曲。

"解出一个已知答案是一回事，提出一个值得被解的新问题是另一回事。AI目前只擅长前者，而科学的进步依赖后者。"—— 声明核心论点

AI行业的回应压力

25位菲尔兹奖得主的联署，给AI行业带来了不小的舆论压力。

这可能是有史以来学术界对AI benchmark文化最权威、最集中的批评。菲尔兹奖得主不是反对AI——很多人在自己的研究中使用AI工具。他们反对的是将AI在数学中的价值等同于"解题得分"的单一叙事。

对AI实验室来说，这份声明提出了一个尖锐的问题：当你宣布"AI攻克了X难题"时，你是在推动科学进步，还是在制造PR素材？当你用benchmark分数来证明AI的价值时，你是在衡量真正重要的东西，还是在自说自话？

这些问题没有简单的答案。但当全球最顶尖的数学集体说"你们搞错了方向"时，AI行业至少应该停下来听一听。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
Solving an answer and truly understanding are two completely different things. Twenty-five of the world's most elite mathematicians just collectively issued that warning to the AI industry.

On September 11, mathematician Terence Tao published a statement on his blog — "A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics" — simultaneously posted to mathandai.org. Within one week, the statement gathered 25 Fields Medal co-signatories. The Fields Medal is the Nobel Prize of mathematics, awarded every four years to at most four people. Twenty-five co-signatories means nearly one-third of all living Fields Medalists stood on the same side.

Core Charge: Benchmark Races ≠ Mathematical Progress

The statement's core argument in one sentence: AI labs treating math problems as benchmark competitions is "severely misaligned" with the actual goals of mathematics as a discipline.

Specifically, here's what AI labs do: select mathematically hard problems with known solutions (competition problems, classical theorem proofs), train AI models to "crack" them, then claim score improvements on leaderboards. But the real goal of mathematical research isn't solving problems with known answers — it's posing new questions, discovering new structures, establishing new connections.

The statement argues that benchmark-driven AI research is creating a dangerous illusion: AI "solves" math problems without advancing mathematics as a discipline. It's more like an extraordinarily powerful exam machine than a creative research partner.

Timing: Navier-Stokes Millennium Problem

The statement's release timing is rather intriguing.

Just three days earlier, on September 8, OpenAI announced it had used 10,000 AI agents to "crack" the Navier-Stokes equations Millennium Problem. OpenAI claimed these agents achieved "substantial progress" on this century-old unsolved problem in hours. The announcement generated enormous media buzz — headlines about "AI solving a Millennium Problem" were everywhere.

Three days later, the Fields Medal laureates' statement arrived. While it doesn't name OpenAI directly, the timing speaks for itself. Using 10,000 agents to brute-force search for a "solution" to a math problem is fundamentally different from truly understanding that problem's essence.

Beyond Math: A Warning Signal for Knowledge Production

Though framed around mathematics, the statement explicitly notes: this problem isn't limited to math.

The same misalignment is happening in every field AI has "cracked" — protein folding, drug discovery, materials science, code generation. AI labs use benchmark scores to prove AI "surpasses humans" in these areas, but benchmarks measure "ability to solve known problems," not "ability to advance a discipline."

The statement argues this threatens broader intellectual work. If AI research direction is held hostage by benchmarks, then truly creative, non-standardized knowledge production gets marginalized. The mathematicians aren't just worried about math's future — they're worried about the entire knowledge production system being warped by an "exam logic."

"Solving a known answer is one thing; posing a new question worth solving is another. AI currently excels only at the former, while scientific progress depends on the latter."— Core thesis of the statement

Pressure on the AI Industry

The co-signature of 25 Fields Medal laureates places significant public pressure on the AI industry.

This may be the most authoritative and concentrated critique of AI benchmark culture from academia in history. The Fields Medalists aren't anti-AI — many use AI tools in their own research. What they oppose is the singular narrative equating AI's value in math with "problem-solving scores."

For AI labs, the statement poses a sharp question: when you announce "AI cracked Problem X," are you advancing science or generating PR material? When you use benchmark scores to prove AI's value, are you measuring something that matters, or talking to yourselves?

These questions have no easy answers. But when the world's most elite mathematicians collectively say "you're heading in the wrong direction," the AI industry should at least stop and listen.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
一台人形机器人在没有人工干预的情况下，从产线末端自主站起、转身、迈步走了下来。这不是实验室视频，而是9月8日小鹏机器人生产线正式启用时的真实场景。全球首条高阶通用人形机器人自动化产线，就这样用一个动作完成了亮相。

从造车到造机器人：特斯拉路线的中国翻版

小鹏的路径几乎是特斯拉Optimus的中国翻版——先用汽车业务积累资金、供应链和制造经验，再横向迁移到人形机器人。8月25日，小鹏机器人业务完成首轮融资，金额超过9亿美元。这个数字说明资本市场定价的不是一款机器人，而是小鹏能否把汽车制造的规模化能力复制到机器人领域。

造车和造机器人之间的技术栈重叠远比外界想象的大。汽车产线上的视觉检测、力控装配、运动规划，和人形机器人的核心能力高度同源。区别在于，汽车制造经过上百年的工程优化，产线良率和效率已被锤炼到极致；而人形机器人制造还处于"能不能造出来"的阶段。小鹏在此时启用专用产线，意味着他们判断技术成熟度已经跨过了"能不能批量造"的门槛。

自动化率80%：产线本身也是技术验证

首台IRON完成全流程自动化总装，自动化率超过80%。这个数字值得关注——即使是高度自动化的汽车产线，装配环节的自动化率也不过如此。人形机器人的零部件复杂度更高，关节、传感器、执行器的精密装配对产线的要求远超消费电子。

小鹏的策略很聪明：用自动化产线造自动化设备，这本身就是一个递归式的技术验证。产线上的每一个装配环节，都在反向验证IRON的设计是否适合批量制造。这种"制造倒逼设计"的逻辑，正是特斯拉从Roadster到Model 3总结出的核心经验。

时间表与全球野心

按照规划，2026年底启动量产，2027年面向中国及海外市场交付。从产线启用到正式交付，留有大约一年的产能爬坡期。

国内市场自不必说，但"海外市场"才是真正的野心所在。人形机器人的全球竞争格局正在快速成形：特斯拉Optimus持续推进、Figure融资上市、1X在欧洲扩张。小鹏要做的不只是在中国卖机器人，而是要在全球舞台上和这些玩家同台竞技。

"自主走下产线"这个画面，是具身智能从demo走向产业化的最佳隐喻——它不再是一个被人类摆弄的展示品，而是一个能够自主行动的产品。但画面之外，真正的挑战才刚刚开始：成本控制、可靠性验证、商业模式探索，每一步都比"走下产线"难得多。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
A humanoid robot stood up at the end of the production line, turned around, and walked off on its own. No human touched it. No remote control guided it. This wasn't a lab demo or a product launch video — it happened on September 8th, when XPeng's humanoid robot production line officially went live. The world's first high-end general-purpose humanoid robot automated assembly line announced itself with the most dramatic possible opening act: its first product autonomously walking away.

From Building Cars to Building Robots: Tesla's Playbook, China Edition

XPeng's trajectory is practically a Chinese clone of Tesla's Optimus playbook — accumulate capital, supply chain expertise, and manufacturing chops through the auto business, then pivot those capabilities sideways into humanoid robots. On August 25, XPeng's robotics division closed its first funding round at over $900 million. That number tells you what the market is pricing in: not one robot, but whether XPeng can transplant automotive-scale manufacturing into the robotics world.

The tech stack overlap between building cars and building robots is far larger than most people assume. Visual inspection, force-controlled assembly, motion planning — these are core capabilities in both domains. The difference is that automotive manufacturing has been optimized over a century of engineering; humanoid robot manufacturing is still in the "can we even build it" phase. XPeng's decision to open a dedicated production line now signals their judgment that the technology has crossed from "buildable" to "batch-producible."

80% Automation: The Production Line as Its Own Proof of Concept

The first IRON completed full-process automated assembly at over 80% automation. That number deserves attention — even highly automated automotive assembly lines achieve comparable rates, and humanoid robots are far more complex. The precision assembly required for joints, sensors, and actuators puts demands on a production line that dwarf those of consumer electronics.

XPeng's strategy is elegant: use an automated production line to build automated equipment — a recursive proof of concept. Every assembly step on the line validates whether IRON's design is actually suited for mass production. This "manufacturing drives design" logic is the core lesson Tesla distilled from its Roadster-to-Model 3 journey.

Timeline and Global Ambitions

XPeng plans to begin mass production by the end of 2026, with deliveries to Chinese and overseas markets starting in 2027. That gives roughly a year to ramp up capacity from line activation to commercial delivery.

The domestic market is a given, but those two words — "overseas markets" — reveal the real ambition. The global humanoid robot competitive landscape is forming fast: Tesla Optimus pushing ahead in the US, Figure going public, 1X expanding across Europe. XPeng isn't just looking to sell robots in China — it's gearing up to compete on the world stage against all of them.

The image of a robot "walking itself off the production line" is, in a sense, the perfect metaphor for embodied AI transitioning from demo to industrialization — it's no longer a display piece humans manipulate, but a product capable of autonomous action. But beyond the optics, the real challenges are only beginning: cost control, reliability validation, business model exploration — every step far harder than walking off a production line.

See you tomorrow.

Quanta Magazine - Mathematicians Question AI-Generated Navier-Stokes Proof
Nature - 25 Fields Medalists warn against AI in mathematics

briefs.body_html:
10,000个AI Agent同时运行，88小时不间断工作，生成270万条Agent间消息，消耗约1300亿输出token。这不是科幻小说里的设定，而是OpenAI在9月8日公布的一次真实计算任务——用AI Agent Swarm对纳维-斯托克斯方程的存在性与光滑性问题给出形式化证明。

史上最大规模的Agent协同实验

纳维-斯托克斯方程是描述流体运动的基本方程，属于Clay数学研究所公布的七大千禧年难题之一，悬赏100万美元。近200年来，数学家们始终无法证明其解在三维空间中是否总是存在且光滑。OpenAI声称，他们的Agent Swarm做到了。

具体来看这次任务的规模：约10,000个并发Agent组成协作网络，每个Agent负责证明链中的不同环节，相互验证、相互修正，历时88小时产出了一份完整的证明草案。随后，Lean形式化验证系统由GPT-6 Astra执行，耗时17小时完成形式化检查。值得注意的是，Agent Swarm使用的并非GPT-6 Astra，而是OpenAI内部一个未公开的、能力更强的模型。

数学界的冷淡与菲尔兹奖得主的警告

OpenAI在声明中明确表示不会申请100万美元千禧年大奖。但即便如此，数学界的反应并不热烈。多位数学家指出，Agent Swarm生成的证明在技术路线和关键引理的合理性上仍需大量人工审核。"通过形式化验证"和"数学上正确"之间还有很大距离——Lean可以检查逻辑链条的一致性，但它无法判断证明的出发点是否有意义。

更耐人寻味的是后续事件。仅仅三天后（9月11日），25位菲尔兹奖得主联合发表声明，警告AI正在"侵入"数学领域。声明并未直接点名OpenAI，但时间节点的巧合已经说明了一切。这些数学家担忧的核心问题不是AI能不能解题，而是AI参与数学研究的方式是否会削弱人类对"理解"的追求。

解题不等于理解：真正的千禧年难题

这次实验最大的技术价值，或许不在于纳维-斯托克斯本身，而在于它验证了Agent Swarm在超大规模复杂任务中的可行性。10,000个并发Agent、1300亿token的协调成本、88小时的持续运行——这套基础设施已经远超任何单一模型的能力边界。它更像是一个分布式计算系统，而不是传统意义上的AI推理。

但"能用Agent Swarm暴力攻下一个数学难题"和"AI理解了流体力学"之间，隔着一个根本性的认知鸿沟。数学家追求的从来不只是正确的答案，而是答案背后的直觉、美感和洞察力。一个由10,000个Agent拼接出来的证明，即使逻辑无懈可击，也很难成为人类数学家灵感的源泉。

OpenAI证明了Agent可以"解题"。但数学界真正关心的"理解"，仍然是一个只有人类才能回答的千禧年难题。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
10,000 AI agents running simultaneously. 88 hours of nonstop work. 2.7 million inter-agent messages. Roughly 130 billion output tokens consumed. This isn't science fiction — it's what OpenAI revealed on September 8th: a real computational exercise using an AI Agent Swarm to produce a formal proof of the Navier-Stokes equations' existence and smoothness problem.

The Largest Agent Collaboration Experiment in History

The Navier-Stokes equations describe fluid motion and sit among the seven Millennium Prize Problems posed by the Clay Mathematics Institute, each carrying a $1 million bounty. For nearly 200 years, mathematicians have been unable to prove that solutions always exist and remain smooth in three dimensions. OpenAI claims their Agent Swarm just did it.

The scale is staggering: roughly 10,000 concurrent agents formed a collaborative network, each handling different segments of the proof chain — verifying each other, correcting each other — working for 88 hours to produce a complete proof draft. Then Lean formal verification, executed by GPT-6 Astra, ran for 17 hours to complete formal checking. Notably, the Agent Swarm didn't use GPT-6 Astra — it used an undisclosed, more powerful internal model.

Math World's Cold Shoulder and a Fields Medal Warning

OpenAI explicitly stated it would not claim the $1 million Millennium Prize. Even so, the math community's response has been tepid. Multiple mathematicians pointed out that the Agent Swarm's proof still requires extensive human review of the technical approach and the validity of key lemmas. "Passes formal verification" and "mathematically correct" remain very different things — Lean can check logical consistency, but it can't judge whether the starting point is meaningful.

What happened next was even more telling. Just three days later (September 11), 25 Fields Medalists issued a joint statement warning that AI is "encroaching on" mathematics. The statement didn't name OpenAI directly, but the timing spoke volumes. Their core concern isn't whether AI can solve problems — it's whether AI's involvement in math research undermines the human pursuit of "understanding."

Solving ≠ Understanding: The Real Millennium Problem

Perhaps the biggest technical takeaway has nothing to do with Navier-Stokes itself, but with the proof that Agent Swarm works at extreme scale for complex tasks. 10,000 concurrent agents, 130 billion tokens of coordination overhead, 88 hours of sustained runtime — this infrastructure already exceeds the capability boundary of any single model. It's closer to a distributed computing system than traditional AI reasoning.

But between "an Agent Swarm can brute-force a math problem" and "AI understands fluid dynamics" lies a fundamental cognitive gap. Mathematicians never pursued just the correct answer — they pursued the intuition, beauty, and insight behind it. A proof stitched together by 10,000 agents, even if logically airtight, is unlikely to become a wellspring of inspiration for human mathematicians.

OpenAI proved that agents can "solve problems." But the "understanding" that mathematicians actually care about remains a millennium problem only humans can answer.

See you tomorrow.

briefs.body_html:
1.4万平方米的厂房里，Walker S系列人形机器人正在组装下一代Walker S系列人形机器人。9月12日，柳州优必选工业人形机器人超级智慧工厂正式投产，广西首个"用机器人造机器人"的闭环制造体系开始运转。这是全球首个适配万台级产能的人形机器人智能制造工厂。

从首台到万台：一年多跑完的产业跳跃

回顾优必选的时间线，速度令人侧目。从首台Walker S原型机突破，到千台级小批量产，再到如今万台级产能的工厂投产，整个过程仅用了一年多。对比汽车行业从原型到量产动辄三到五年的周期，这个速度几乎是压缩了两到三倍。

快速的背后有两层原因。第一，人形机器人的零部件供应链和工业机器人、自动化设备高度重叠，优必选作为中国人形机器人头部公司，供应链积累已经超过十年。第二，柳州的选择并非偶然——广西是中国面向东盟的制造业门户，土地、人工、政策成本都远低于一线城市，而当地完善的汽车产业配套可以直接服务于机器人制造。

"用机器人造机器人"：不只是宣传口号

"用机器人造机器人"听起来像营销话术，但在工程层面它意味着一个关键的能力闭环：你造出的机器人足够可靠，可以胜任精密制造任务；你的产线足够成熟，能容纳自家产品的自动化装配。这两件事同时成立，才是真正的技术门槛。

工厂主要生产Walker S系列和Cruzr系列，前者面向工业场景（巡检、搬运、装配），后者面向服务场景（导览、接待）。两个系列共享大量底层模块化设计，使得同一产线可以灵活切换产品型号。这对万台级产能的工厂至关重要——没有足够的产线灵活性，万台级产能反而会成为库存负担。

规模化量产：具身智能的真正分水岭

如果说小鹏IRON代表了"造车公司跨界造机器人"的路径，那么优必选代表的是另一条路：专业机器人公司的规模化。前者的优势在于汽车制造经验和资金实力，后者的优势在于十年以上的人形机器人技术积累和对行业的深度理解。

两条路径的共同指向是：具身智能正在从实验室走向工厂，从demo走向量产。万台级产能不是终点，而是一个信号——当产能突破万台，人形机器人的单位成本才有可能降到企业客户愿意大规模采购的区间。

柳州工厂的投产，标志着具身智能正式进入规模化量产阶段。但"投产"和"满产"之间还有很长的路要走。订单能否填满产能，良率能否维持高位，海外市场能否打开——这些问题的答案，将在未来12个月内逐步揭晓。

明天见。
briefs.body_html_en:
Inside a 14,000-square-meter factory, Walker S humanoid robots are assembling the next generation of Walker S humanoid robots. On September 12, UBTECH's Liuzhou Industrial Humanoid Robot Super Smart Factory officially opened — Guangxi's first closed-loop manufacturing system where "robots build robots." It's the world's first smart manufacturing facility designed for 10,000-unit humanoid robot capacity.

From First Unit to Ten Thousand: An Industrial Leap in Just Over a Year

UBTECH's timeline is striking. From the first Walker S prototype breakthrough, to small-batch production of hundreds, to today's 10,000-unit-capacity factory — the entire arc took just over a year. Compared to the three-to-five-year cycle typical for automobiles from prototype to mass production, this pace is compressed by two to three times.

Two factors explain the speed. First, humanoid robot component supply chains heavily overlap with industrial robotics and automation equipment. As China's leading humanoid robot company, UBTECH has over a decade of supply chain accumulation. Second, Liuzhou wasn't a random choice — Guangxi is China's manufacturing gateway to ASEAN, with land, labor, and policy costs far below first-tier cities, while the local automotive industry infrastructure directly serves robot manufacturing.

'Robots Building Robots': More Than a Marketing Line

The factory primarily produces Walker S series (for industrial scenarios: inspection, transport, assembly) and Cruzr series (for service scenarios: reception, wayfinding). Both lines share extensive modular base designs, allowing flexible product switching on the same line. Mass Production: Embodied AI's Real Watershed

The Liuzhou factory's opening marks embodied AI's official entry into scaled mass production. But between "open" and "full capacity" lies a long road. Whether orders can fill capacity, whether yields stay high, whether overseas markets open — the answers will unfold over the next 12 months.

cao.body_html:
朋友们，今天主角叫Stephen D. Aarons，新墨西哥州的一位律师。他用ChatGPT帮自己写一份谋杀案的上诉brief。高效是真高效——ChatGPT在brief里给他编了4个完全虚构的证人、若干段从未发生过的证词，以及一堆根本不存在的法律引用。

法庭：你当我这是小说发布会？

新墨西哥州最高法院的法官看到这份brief时，大概经历了以下心路历程：先是困惑（"这个案例我怎么没读过？"），然后是怀疑（"让我查一下……"），最后是愤怒（"这些都是假的"）。

结果很干脆：法院判定Aarons藐视法庭，罚款5000美元，禁止他在新墨西哥州最高法院出庭，那份brief被从案件记录中彻底删除。更惨的是他的当事人——被告Oscar Renee Sandoval的谋杀案上诉被迫中止，法院需要重新指定律师从头来过。

这不是第一次了

如果Aarons做过功课，他应该知道2023年纽约就有律师犯过完全相同的错误：用ChatGPT撰写法律文件，被发现包含虚构案例引用，被法官训斥。当时这个新闻铺天盖地，整个法律界都在讨论。

但Aarons显然觉得"我的情况不会那么糟"。这种心态很普遍——很多人用ChatGPT时抱着微妙的侥幸心理：它可能出错，但不会在我的任务上出错。低风险场景下无伤大雅，但当你面对的是法庭、谋杀案、一个人的自由时，侥幸心理就是渎职。

AI能当助手，不能替你做决定

AI在法律研究、文件审阅、合同分析上已证明了价值。关键区别在于：AI做辅助工作，不替代判断。

让ChatGPT帮你梳理案件逻辑、整理法律条文、优化文书表达——没问题。但让ChatGPT"帮你找到支持论点的案例"——这就是灾难的起点。因为它找不到合适的案例时，不会告诉你"没有"，它会一本正经地编一个。这不是bug，是语言模型的本质：它生成最可能的下一个token，而不是最正确的下一个事实。

给用AI工具的朋友们三条提醒：

第一，AI生成的每一个事实性引用——案例、数据、人物、引文——都必须手动验证，没有例外。

第二，如果AI"找不到"你需要的素材却仍给出像样的答案，大概率是编的。真正诚实的回答是"我不知道"。

第三，在任何有法律、医疗、财务后果的场景中使用AI，一定要有人类审核环节。不是"最好有人审核"，是必须有人审核。

今天就槽到这里，明天继续。
cao.body_html_en:
Friends, allow me to introduce today's protagonist: Stephen D. Aarons, a New Mexico lawyer who decided to embrace the future of legal practice. He used ChatGPT to draft a murder appeal brief. Efficient? Absolutely. ChatGPT produced 4 entirely fictional witnesses, several fabricated testimonies, and a collection of legal citations that exist in no law library on Earth.

The Court: You Think This Is a Book Launch?

When the New Mexico Supreme Court justices read this brief, they probably went through a predictable emotional journey: confusion ("I don't recognize this case..."), then suspicion ("Let me look that up..."), then fury ("None of this is real.").

The verdict was swift: Aarons was found in contempt of court, fined $5,000, barred from practicing before the New Mexico Supreme Court, and the fantasy-filled brief was stricken from the record entirely. The real victim? His client — accused murderer Oscar Renee Sandoval's appeal was halted, and the court had to appoint a new lawyer to start from scratch.

One man's freedom, delayed by another man's shortcut.

This Isn't the First Time, Friends

If Aarons had done even minimal homework, he'd know that a New York lawyer pulled the exact same stunt in 2023. That attorney also used ChatGPT for legal filings, also got caught with fabricated case citations, also got chewed out by a judge. It was front-page news across the entire legal profession.

But Aarons either didn't notice, or he noticed and thought, "That won't happen to me." This mindset is surprisingly common. Many people use ChatGPT with a quiet sense of immunity: sure, it makes mistakes, but probably not on my task. In low-stakes scenarios, that's harmless. But when you're dealing with a court of law, a murder case, and a person's freedom, false confidence isn't confidence — it's malpractice.

AI Can Be Your Assistant, Not Your Decision-Maker

I'm not here to trash AI in the legal field. In fact, AI has already proven its worth in legal research, document review, and contract analysis. The critical distinction: AI does support work. It doesn't replace judgment.

Having ChatGPT help you organize case logic, compile existing statutes, polish your brief's language — all fine. But asking ChatGPT to "find cases that support my argument" — that's where the disaster starts. When ChatGPT can't find a relevant case, it won't tell you "I don't have one." It'll fabricate one with complete confidence. This isn't a bug — it's the fundamental nature of language models: they generate the most probable next token, not the most truthful next fact.

For all my friends using AI tools, three reminders:

First, every factual claim AI generates — cases, data, names, quotes — must be manually verified. No exceptions. Ever.

Second, if AI can't find what you're looking for but still gives you a polished answer, it's almost certainly making it up. The truly honest response would be "I don't know."

Third, in any scenario with legal, medical, or financial consequences, there must be a human review step. Not "ideally" — mandatorily.

That's all the roasting for today. More tomorrow.
